text:
alice: anyone else seeing weird churn in the us-west1 gpu pools this morning? HPA + CA are dancing — replicas go up, CA adds nodes, nodes get removed, pods evicted, tail latency spikes.
ben: yup saw alerts. grafana shows the custom metric `gpu_queue_qps` oscillating every ~40s. CA scale-down logs show nodes marked unneeded then removed quickly.
carla: are these on the preemptible nodepool or the on-demand one? preemptible churn would explain a lot.
dmitri: looks like both. we have gpu-preemptible and gpu-standard nodepools. CA prefers preemptible first but when preemptible drains pods onto standard, the HPA sees per-pod qps jump and immediately scales again -> loop.
alice: that's the hypothesis. HPA is configured to target per-pod QPS (external metric from our queue-proxy) which means when replicas collapse onto fewer pods qps_per_pod spikes and HPA ups reps. CA reacts and provisions nodes -> pods spread -> per-pod qps drops -> HPA scales down -> repeat.
ben: quick actionable checks: `kubectl describe hpa model-serve` and `kubectl get --all-namespaces vpa` to see if VPA is updating requests. Also `kubectl get nodes -l cloud.google.com/gke-nodepool=gpu-preemptible -o wide`.
carla: note: we have VPA running in auto for some model-serving deployments. VPA writing new requests can trigger pod restarts/rolling updates which makes HPA/CA see transient load. For GPU workloads I recommend VPA updateMode: "Off" or Recommendation only.
dmitri: additional contributor: HPA behavior (scaleUp/stabilization) is default. we don't have stabilizationWindowSeconds tuned. set behavior.stabilizationWindowSeconds: 300 for both up/down to dampen quick oscillations. also set minReplicas: 2 for critical models so CA doesn't scale nodepool to 0.
alice: good call. also our CA scale-down-unneeded-time is 10m but scale-down-delay-after-add is low; if CA thinks nodes are unneeded quickly it can remove them soon after add. maybe bump `--scale-down-unneeded-time` and `--scale-down-delay-after-add` for gpu-preemptible pool.
ben: another option: switch HPA to aggregate metric (total queue length) rather than per-pod QPS. then HPA won't overreact to replica redistribution. KEDA + external scaler for Redis/RabbitMQ queue length works well here.
carla: also add a PodDisruptionBudget for model-serving so CA doesn't evict too many pods at once, and use priorityClass for critical workloads so preemptible pool doesn't steal them.
infra-bot: [cluster-events] nodepool/gpu-preemptible scaled from 0 -> 4 (provisioning), node/gke-gpu-pp-1 started, pod/model-serve-abc scheduled on node/gke-gpu-pp-1
ben: sample commands to run: ```
kubectl describe hpa model-serve -n prod
kubectl get hpa -n prod -o yaml
kubectl get vpa -n prod -o yaml
kubectl get pods -n prod -l app=model-serve -o wide
kubectl get nodes -l cloud.google.com/gke-nodepool=gpu-preemptible
```
dmitri: longer term: 1) stop using per-pod qps as the HPA metric for bursty workloads, 2) prefer global queue metrics or hybrid (queue length + cpu/gpu util), 3) avoid VPA auto-updates on GPU apps, 4) set CA expander strategy to prefer on-demand for critical pools.
alice: i'm going to apply a hotfix: set HPA.behavior.stabilizationWindowSeconds=300 and minReplicas=2, disable VPA updateMode for these deployments, and add PDB. I'll also pin the most latency-sensitive model to gpu-standard for now.
carla: i'll open an infra PR to increase scale-down delays for gpu-preemptible and add a note about expander behavior.
ben: remember to adjust our cost dashboard — keeping minReplicas=2 and more on-demand will raise short-term cost. include cost delta in the PR description.
dmitri: i'll handle converting the HPA metric to global queue length and propose a KEDA ScaledObject if the team wants it.
alice: assigning follow-ups: @dmitri metric switch, @carla CA config PR, @alice hotfix + runbook. please ping on this thread when changes land.
carla: one more gotcha we saw earlier: VPA sometimes patches `spec.template.spec.containers[].resources.requests` which triggers a rolling update. for GPU pods that can kill the only scheduled pod on a node and temporarily spike per-pod qps — disable updates or add `resourcePolicy` to exclude gpu requests.
ben: +1 on resourcePolicy. also consider a small HPA tolerance band or use metrics-server smoothing to reduce jitter.
alice: thanks all. i'll implement hotfix now and post results. :thumbsup:
